content: 1. Levofloxacin displaces GABA from its receptors in the brain, which can lead to central nervous system (CNS) stimulation or seizures. This mechanism is particularly relevant when combined with other drugs that may exacerbate this effect. 2. Drugs such as ibutilide and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use alternative medications. 3. Iloperidone and levofloxacin also increase the QTc interval. Close monitoring is advised if these drugs are used together. 4. Imipramine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 5. Indacaterol (inhaled) and levofloxacin can increase the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 6. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval, such as levofloxacin, may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias, including torsades de pointes. 7. Indapamide and levofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 8. Levofloxacin and indomethacin may interact, requiring close monitoring. The risk of CNS stimulation or seizures is a concern. 9. Inotuzumab and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and during treatment. 10. Levofloxacin increases the effects of insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic synergy. This may result in hyperor hypoglycemia. Close monitoring is required. 11. Quinolone antibiotics, including levofloxacin, may cause dysglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause this, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 12. Levofloxacin increases the effects of insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, insulin lispro, and insulin NPH through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely for hyperor hypoglycemia. 13. Iron dextran complex and iron sucrose decrease the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Isoflurane and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 15. Levofloxacin and isotretinoin may increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Itraconazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Ivosidenib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. 18. Ketoconazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 19. Levofloxacin and ketoprofen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 20. Lanthanum carbonate decreases levofloxacin levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer oral quinolones at least 1 hour before or 4 hours after lanthanum. 21. Lapatinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Lefamulin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 23. Levofloxacin and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 24. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of oral contraceptives (e.g., levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol) by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution is advised. 26. Lithium and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Lofepramine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 28. Levofloxacin increases the levels of benzodiazepines such as loprazolam, lorazepam, and lormetazepam by decreasing their metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Levofloxacin and lornoxicam may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 30. Levofloxacin and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 31. Macimorelin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 32. Magnesium salts (e.g., magnesium chloride, citrate, hydroxide, oxide, sulfate) decrease levofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or after levofloxacin. 33. Maprotiline and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 34. Mavorixafor and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc during treatment, especially in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. 35. Levofloxacin and meclofenamate may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 36. Levofloxacin and mefenamic acid may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 37. Levofloxacin and meloxicam may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 38. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution is advised. 39. Levofloxacin increases the effects of metformin and miglitol through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely for hyperor hypoglycemia. 40. Levofloxacin and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Levofloxacin and methyl aminolevulinate may increase each other's phototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 42. Levofloxacin and methylprednisolone may increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Levofloxacin decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota. 44. Levofloxacin increases the levels of midazolam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Mifepristone and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use alternatives if available, and monitor closely. 46. Mirtazapine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Levofloxacin and mometasone (inhaled) may increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Levofloxacin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 49. Levofloxacin and nabumetone may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 50. Levofloxacin and naproxen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 51. Levofloxacin increases the effects of nateglinide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely for hyperor hypoglycemia. 52. Levofloxacin and nilotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 53. Nortriptyline and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 54. Levofloxacin and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 55. Levofloxacin and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Olanzapine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Levofloxacin and olodaterol (inhaled) both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Ondansetron and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. ECG monitoring is recommended in patients with congenital long QT syndrome or other risk factors. 59. Osilodrostat and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Osimertinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Conduct periodic ECG and electrolyte monitoring in patients taking QT-prolonging drugs. 61. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of levofloxacin. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, so avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 62. Levofloxacin and oxaprozin may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 63. Levofloxacin increases the levels of oxazepam by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 64. Ozanimod and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
